data.exact_reserve_text: An overall improvement of GBP 5.0 million on prior years' provisions was experienced during the year. Improvements of GBP 0.9 million on motor, GBP 16.9 million on fire and other damage to property and GBP 2.2 million on pecuniary loss were partially offset by deteriorations of GBP 6.0 million on third party liability, GBP 2.5 million on energy, GBP 3.3 million on reinsurance acceptances and GBP 3.0 million on marine, aviation and transport.

prior_year_events.event_name: CG Restaurants & Bars v RSA (and Stonegate v MS Amlin)
prior_year_events.impact_description: New court cases expected to challenge the basis upon which business interruption claims have been paid; contributed to uncertainty in ultimate outcome for prior years (2018 year closure decision impacted).
Business interruption claims (notably in Australia) have materially affected prior years (2019 year) and remain subject to legal rulings, increasing uncertainty over ultimate liability.

named_events.loss_description: The largest event loss incurred by Syndicate 2121 was from Hurricane Ida that struck the US in August 2021; industry insured loss estimated around US$36 billion. Settlement of claims is taking an inordinately long time; syndicate loss estimates considered robust but finality not reached.
A very severe winter storm and freeze hit the US state of Texas causing around US$15 billion of insured damage; noted as an unusual early-year event for 2021.
Extremely damaging flood in central Europe in July which caused around US$13 billion of insured damage and up to US$40 billion of economic losses.
Terrible outbreak of tornadoes across the US Mid-West in December 2021 noted among loss events for the year.
A wildfire in Denver in December 2021 noted as an out-of-season event affecting the industry and referenced in the syndicate review.

data.standardized_narrative: Syndicate 2121 reported an overall improvement on prior years' claims provisions of GBP 5.0m in 2021, driven by favourable development in motor (GBP 0.9m), fire and other damage to property (GBP 16.9m) and pecuniary loss (GBP 2.2m), partially offset by adverse development in third party liability (GBP 6.0m), energy (GBP 2.5m), reinsurance acceptances (GBP 3.3m) and marine, aviation and transport (GBP 3.0m). The net prior-year movement is a small release relative to opening gross reserves of GBP 632.1m. Wider drivers of reserve uncertainty noted in the report include COVID-19 business interruption exposures (notably Australia) and emerging court rulings challenging BI claim payments.

gross_premium_mix.line_of_business: Fire and other damage to property

data.data_quality_notes: Prior-year movement taken from the dedicated 'Movement in prior year's provision for claims outstanding' note which states a GBP 5.0m improvement. The note is used as a gross movement source though the narrative does not explicitly label the figure as 'gross' vs 'net' - it is presented in the movement note and assumed gross per standard note context. 'Pecuniary loss' is mapped to 'Professional Lines' for standardized LOB mapping. Claims development triangle present and extracted; aggregate 'Before 2012' column was excluded per instructions.
